body:
Thank you for reporting the issue. We will accept the patch that errors out or documentation update that mentions this behavior: sort is a trivial operation for tensors with less than 2 elements, so it can return self for any dtype.
But sorting does not make sense for complex tensors with more than one element as there are no unambiguous comparison operation for complex numbers

issue.title: `argsort()` can use the 0D tensor of a complex type value against error message

repository.name: pytorch
repository.description: Tensors and Dynamic neural networks in Python with strong GPU acceleration

issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

[argsort()](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.argsort.html) cannot use the tensor of `complex` type values according to the error message as shown below:

```python
import torch

my_tensor = torch.tensor([7.+5.j])

torch.argsort(input=my_tensor) # Error

my_tensor = torch.tensor([[7.+5.j]])

torch.argsort(input=my_tensor) # Error
```

> RuntimeError: "sorting_kernel_method_name" not implemented for 'ComplexFloat'

But `argsort()` can use the 0D tensor of a `complex` type value against the error message as shown below:

```python
import torch

my_tensor = torch.tensor(7.+5.j)

torch.argsort(input=my_tensor)
# tensor(0)
```


### Versions

```python
import torch

torch.__version__ # 2.3.0+cu121
```
